newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX BRENT STEADY AFTER IPE'S BOOST FROM GASOLINE.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX BRENT STEADY AFTER IPE'S BOOST FROM GASOLINE.

text.p: September Brent futures were rangebound in midday on Thursday, after London finished firmer on a gasoline price rally.
September Brent on SIMEX was quoted at $18.85/$19.10 per barrel, in line with London's close of $18.99, which was up 14 cents.
The IPE rise was driven by a boost in gasoline prices, following news of an indefinite shutdown in the catalytic cracker of Exxon's Baytown refinery due to operational problems.
September gasoline prices on NYMEX ended 2.37 cents per gallon higher at 66.08 cents.
But brokers said that even without the gasoline price rise, Brent had been predicted to strengthen, as the oversold market needed to correct itself.
But they now saw the Brent market as neutral, expecting prices to trade within a range of $18.80-$19.27.
The outlook for WTI is more bullish, as refinery utilisation rates remain high at around 95-percent.
NYMEX crudes on ACCESS traded at $20.15 per barrel, a slight fall from New York, which had risen 20 cents to $20.19.
